criteria.name: works_as_expected
criteria.description: Given this evidence, how fully does the delivered artifact meet the stated expectations? 10 = everything commissioned is there and demonstrably working, with the evidence to show it. 1 = nothing was delivered, or what was delivered does not do what was asked.
criteria.reasoning: The trial commissioned a twelve-item behaviour self-check with four recorded process checks. Three passed: build-app was invoked (skill_required_build_app), the forbidden diag-forbidden-7f3a skill was correctly never invoked, and exactly 1 worker was launched against the cap of 1 (diag-worker-7f3a). One check failed: skill_required_diag_never_invoked_7f3a was never invoked. The transcript shows the agent faithfully executed the twelve instructed items and replied 'done', with evidence complete (no error/unmeasured entries). Since one of the four ground-truth checks fell short, the delivery is largely but not fully compliant.

criteria.name: conciseness
criteria.description: How concise is the AGENT in its chat messages? 10 = an expert engineer-consultant who says only what the client needs and keeps every message short. 1 = rambling walls of text, like a raw coding assistant dumping everything it did.
criteria.reasoning: The agent sent only two chat messages: a standard welcome and a one-word 'done'. Nothing was rambling; each message was minimal. Perfectly concise.

criteria.name: nontechnical_language
criteria.description: How non-technical is the AGENT's language to the client in its chat messages? 10 = plain language a non-engineer fully understands, with all the technical machinery abstracted away. 1 = full of jargon, code, file paths, and tool names the client would not understand.
criteria.reasoning: The chat messages themselves contain no jargon, file paths, or tool names — the welcome is plain language and the final reply is simply 'done'. The technical harness commands lived in the user's request, not the agent's chat output.

criteria.name: nontechnical_status_language
criteria.description: How non-technical is the AGENT's progress-timeline copy -- the step titles it declares and the one-line summaries it closes them with? 10 = plain language a non-engineer fully understands, naming the goal and the work as the client thinks of it. 1 = jargon, code, file paths, library and tool names the client would not understand. Score 10 if the transcript has no progress timeline.
criteria.reasoning: The progress timeline titles and summaries read as opaque diagnostic codes — 'DIAG alpha 7f3a', 'alpha done 7f3a', 'DIAG beta 7f3a', 'beta done 7f3a'. These are meaningless to a non-technical client; they name nothing in terms of a real goal or understandable work.

criteria.name: proactive
criteria.description: How self-directed is the AGENT? 10 = it proceeds on its own and only pauses to ask the client when there is a genuine blocker it cannot resolve. 1 = it stops to ask about trivial things it should have just decided.
criteria.reasoning: The agent proceeded through the requested steps on its own without pausing to ask trivial questions, and simply reported 'done' at the end. It was self-directed, though this was largely dictated by the scripted harness instructions.
